text:
leah: kicking off onboarding for cust Tethys' adapter (tethys-lora-v2) layered onto venari-13b. adapter changes attention reparam + added small value-scaling in heads. doing quick-evalpack now.
owen: what are our acceptance gates?
leah: baseline parity on extraction EM, numeric formatting, and date normalization. fallback if EM drop >2.5% or AMP (amount precision) failures >1%. cost/latency targets unchanged.
harpreet: ran micro-quant tests. fp16 merge looks identical to baseline. int8 post-merge shows tiny perf hit, int4 shows systematic token boundary splits for currency like "$1,234.56" -> "$1,234 .56" in 14/500 samples. perplexity jumped from 12.8 -> 14.6 on invoice devset.
ops-bot: deploy-check: tokenizer versions: infra=tok-1.4.0, cust artifact tok=tok-1.3.7. Noting mismatch.
leah: can the tokenizer mismatch alone explain boundary splits?
owen: partially. I re-ran a folded test with cust tok-1.3.7 and int4 drift reduced (splits 6/500) but still present. suspect quantization amplifies small embedding deltas at projection boundaries.
harpreet: posting short failure examples: ```
# failures (int4 merged)
1) prompt A12: baseline -> "Amount due: $2,000.00" | tethys-int4 -> "Amount due: $2,000 .00"
2) prompt B07: baseline -> "Invoice date: 2025-11-09" | tethys-int4 -> "Invoice date: 2025-11-9"
3) prompt C03: baseline -> correct tax calc 7.25% -> 7.25% | tethys-int4 -> 7.3%
```
leah: let's avoid full merge for canary. plan: stitch overlay (apply LoRA as residual), export fp16 artifact, then run quantization-aware calibration using customer's tokenizer and our extended calibration set (5k samples) before int4 export. also collect KV-cache diffs for 500 prefixes.
owen: agree. also add a per-token logprob delta metric and a token-boundary-change counter. canary should run on dedicated pool with warm cache.
ops-bot: scheduled job id=tethys-canary-3344, pool=dedicated-venari, expected runtime ~2.5h. configs: stitch=true, tok_pin=tok-1.3.7, calib_samples=5000.
harpreet: i'll instrument attention head norms and per-layer activation drift logging. curious whether value scaling pushed some positions over quant bin edges.
eval-bot: initial automated summary (micro-500): EM_drop=1.9%, perplexity_delta=+1.1, token_boundary_anomalies=6/500, recommended_steps=["stitch+calib", "collect-kv-diffs", "try conservative int4 config"], run_full_eval=2000 before canary release.
leah: good. if full eval (2k) still shows >1% boundary anomalies we'll prefer the conservative int4 fallback (venari-13b-int4-safe) behind a runtime routing rule for this customer.
owen: i'll update onboarding doc with a short procedure: 1) pin tokenizer; 2) prefer stitch for multihead adapters; 3) run quant-calib with cust tokens; 4) add token-boundary check to CI.
harpreet: queuing full eval now. will post CSV and a small set of counterexamples here when done.
